bull.b: Rapid revenue growth combined with a large backlog provides meaningful demand visibility across Launch and Space Systems. More than 45% of backlog is expected to convert within 12 months, supporting continued expansion and giving the company a durable base for scaling operations.

Materially higher gross margins indicate improving unit economics as Rocket Lab scales its integrated launch and space systems operations. Better margins can support reinvestment in production capacity and Neutron development while gradually improving the path toward sustainable profitability.

A strengthened capital structure and substantial liquidity give Rocket Lab flexibility to fund development, infrastructure, acquisitions, and working-capital needs. Very low debt relative to equity also reduces balance-sheet pressure while the company continues investing ahead of broader profitability.

bear.b: Rocket Lab continues to consume substantial cash while funding operations, Neutron development, and investment programs. Persistent negative operating and free cash flow may require ongoing access to capital and limits the company’s ability to finance growth solely from internally generated funds.

Despite strong growth and better gross margins, Rocket Lab has not yet demonstrated sustainable operating or net profitability. Continued losses weaken shareholder returns and leave future earnings dependent on further scale, execution, and successful conversion of backlog into profitable revenue.

Neutron is central to Rocket Lab’s longer-term launch ambitions, but a narrowing launch window and remaining testing and integration milestones create execution risk. Continued elevated capital spending also raises the cost of delay and can prolong cash burn before the program contributes revenue.
